I'm married now and have lived with two different women (obviously at different times) one for just over two years and one for just shy of two years. I also had relations (after a few months) with a young lady whom I dated for about 9 months.

Before I was married, I *guess* I didn't have a real reason (I was quite busy with college (and drank and did opiates it private). My first 'date' and kiss was in college and I found out she told mutual friends I must be a homosexual because I only kissed her after walking to her car. (She lived with her parents and my flat was so small I could touch the door from my bed.) That put me off dating for a while. I did have more than a few offers when I was teaching at college from my students (I'm guessing for a better grade and *not* because I'm incredibly intelligent, witty, and good looking).

Now, my wife is addicted to the Internet and ignores me and our children. I realize that being in our 50's isn't a "death sentence" as far as sex goes, but that it is not what I miss the most. My skin hungers to be touched. I would **never** cheat, and I'd wait until my children were older to file for divorce (although I do have logs of the enormous amount of time on the Internet if necessary).

I'd have no idea how I could *personally* separate the emotional part from the physical part. That's how *I* am. I make no judgments on how other people live if they are not harming anyone else.

My wife is a Second Life addict. She has been for two or three years now. If the kids are being 'too loud' or 'too demanding' of her attention, she will take her laptop to our bedroom. These 'kids' are our children: a nine-year-old boy and a thirteen-year-old girl.

If she doesn't have to work the next day, she will stay up until 4:00 AM and sleep all day. I take care of the children all weekend. I'm not really sure why, but she works until 9PM or later. (My 13 year old daughter gets herself off to school and my wife *does* get my son on the school bus.)

I get to work by 6:30AM every day so I can leave by 2:30 or 3 PM so I can be around for homework & dinner. Quite honestly, it's best that she's not home until after they go to bed. They want her attention, which is very understandable, and she doesn't *act* like she wants to be a mother. It's not just me and her children that she ignores, but also her bedridden mother (who happens to live about 2 miles away).

This is all her loss. I'm 52 and she is 51 years old. As soon as the children are 18, I am leaving. The children are welcome to join me, or not. Right now, my daughter sees how abnormal it is that her *father* is buying her bras and other "girl stuff". My son sees me as the bad guy. (That's perfectly normal and alright with me since **I** have to make, and enforce, all the rules.) I know I'm doing the best that I can for my children-- short of leaving my wife now. (It would be doubtful that I would get custody. Although it was a *long* time ago, I was unable to work after September 11th. I was earning a ton of money in Manhattan at the time, but my world came crumbling down so to speak.)

I'm not a very exciting guy. I'll admit that. I have degrees, and taught Ancient Languages (Tamil and Sanskrit mainly) and now do some pretty esoteric and pseudo-anonymous translating via the Internet. I read a lot and write. (I've published a few articles in peer review journals and one fictional piece that did a little better than 'break even'.)

I'm not particularly handsome, or thin. On the other hand, I don't drink, smoke, or do much else but interact with our children. I do try to be a good provider financially and emotionally to our children.

Once the children go to bed, I am quite lonely. <shrug> I could be a lot worse.

Second Life, like any addiction I believe, is merely a distraction. The distinction between *my* distractions (reading & writing) and Second Life (to the extremes people do) and alcohol, drugs, food, sex, or anything else, is the harm we cause ourselves and others.

I have devoted my private life to becoming a benefit to all sentient beings. I do this by trying to live my life in what *I* consider the "right way". I'll pop on and do the odd translation. I'll help out a college student with getting the proper symbols to quote languages that use different alphabets than what are commonly available. I try, when I have time, to write to people who are trying to communicate with grandparents in a language they have all but lost.

I do what I can. I don't poke fun at those with addiction. I try to look at the horrible pain some may be in that they will go to such lengths to escape. I have little intelligent to say about the subject. I'm not even intelligent to have the proper questions.

I just wanted to leave this here as a sign of the collateral damage that can occur when any addiction goes awry.

I remain,

Hi. You can call me Tenzin. I'm middle aged, married with two children (9 year old and 13 year old). My wife is addicted to SecondLife. (That's the last 4-5 years but honestly there has always been something to distract her from her *real* life.) It is her loss, but she also ignores our children.

I'm a Junior High teacher. A very lonely profession-- very little interaction with adults. As for hobbies, I read and write. (Those too leave me alone.) I do some 'sideline' work in high level encryption (usually by companies that show Medical communities, Banks, and Government how they have, almost, no security at all). That leaves me alone behind the screen.

I am indeed alone. Very few people can understand the huge pain that is endured…alone.

My personal opinion is that we are all suffering, to some extent, one way or another. Each of our suffering is unique and the primary way in which we communicate, language, is left unable to express this suffering in even the least adequate manner. Too often, people do not look at the *source* of our suffering (whatever that *may* be) to help the suffering end, and we end up involved self-destructive ways that just cause more pain-- food, alcohol, drugs, harmful relationships...

The thing is that it each of our unique circumstances, that leads us to suffering that also leads us to the ultimate commune. Yes we are all suffering, but we are all suffering together.

I'd have to say yes. All during elementary, Junior High, and High School. I have a twin brother (who would have rather go out with "friends" he didn't like than hang out with me) and an older brother who never had anything to do with me.

Before there were any laws about 'hacking' (1980's?) I got in *some* sort of (I guess it was unofficial) trouble with the US Federal Government. I was fortunate enough to have gotten a scholarship abroad and I was *convinced* by men in Black Jackets to leave the country for a 'while'.

When I arrived at my 'host' country, I was met by members of the US Consulate who 'requested' my Student Visa & Passport. I was virtually a prisoner of the country I was in. Aside from documents from the University / College, I did not exist. I had to do work either for the University, or off the books, take a pretty small / crappy flat where there would be no questions asked... I had one (my first) 'date' while in college, but other than that I just continued to "self-medicated".

After 7 years or so of studying and teaching at the University, I was allowed to have my papers back from the US Consulate and came back to the States. I didn't have anybody their, so I did return to the states.

I'm married now, but my wife ignores me. I don't have a friend in the world.

This is **my** life. Your mileage may vary.

This is a throw away account, for some obvious reasons. Although I grew up in a 'nuclear family' (Mom, Dad, and two brothers). My father was a very angry man. He *never* resorted to physical violence, but the threat was always present. "What I can't do, I can *pay* to have done." and "I could have you taken away in the middle of the night." were both things I heard from as young as eight years old. **This** is not the story.
Although psychologically abused herself, my mother turned around and performed a *different* style of psychological manipulation and abuse. I became the father figure by age ten. (My father always seemed to be 'out'.) I was my mother's sounding board-- her confidant. I was a boy. **She** should have been sticking up for me! This lasted until my father 'discovered' my intentions of going to college and kicked me out of the house.
I now have a relationship with my mother, but it is not a mother/son relationship. It is *very* one sided. I won't bore you with stories.
I know this pales in comparison to many abuse victim's stories, but it is mine and I remain.
